decided.cycle: A tall weekly bar comes back about every 4.2 weeks (weeks 4, 8, 12/13, 17, 21, 25, 29, 34, 38, 42, 46, 50, 55, 59, 63, 67, 72, 76, 80, 84, 88, 93, 97, 101). Weeks 4 to 101 span 23 intervals, which gives about 29.5 days
decided.week: Each bar is a weekly total, so any pattern inside a week is hidden
decided.level: Ordinary weeks sit around 3500-5000 in the first 52 weeks and around 2500-3500 in weeks 53-104. The peaks are also somewhat lower
decided.year: Weeks 38-46 peak in year 1 and weeks 93/97 peak in year 2, which is a weak match only. The monthly cycle hides any annual pattern
decided.highest_day: Week 42 (days 288-294) has the highest weekly total, but the bars don't show which day in that week
decided.second_day: Can't name a day because the bars only give weekly totals
decided.peak_shape: I can't see daily values inside a weekly bar
decided.drops: No full week falls far below its neighbours. Week 105 is short only because it holds 3 days (729-731), and single-day drops can't be seen in weekly totals
decided.stands_out: The weekly bars that rise above the regular cycle peaks: week 42 (14.4k), week 38 (13.3k), week 93 (12.7k), week 17 (12.1k) and week 46 (11.6k)

answer.guess: Something tied to the lunar cycle (~29.5 days), maybe night-time activity, emergency visits or fishing catches, with a falling trend
